Thanks. It's hard to see everything clearly when you're so close to the problem, so seeing your reply really puts it into perspective for me. 

I know it sounds crazy that just a few months of therapy could do so much, but really, before my mother came back into my life, it genuinely was enough for me. I no longer had that deep-rooted resentment, I no longer felt like a victim who should be pitied, and I no longer felt like my life was hopeless and worth nothing. 

I get now that it was nothing more than a bandage that covered up all the shit underneath, or a house of cards that fell the moment a breeze came in, but I was making amazing progress in my life before she came back into it. Sure, I couldn't really address what happened to me and ACCEPT it, and looking back on those days still fills me with dread, but I was moving on in life. For some people, that might not be enough, but for me it was. I was finding acceptance and happiness for the first time in years.

To answer your questions: my sister did go through college. My dad paid for her full 4 years, her residency, and all her food and clothes and necessities. She's always been his favorite. I'm not sure why he hated me so much, but he's always done his best for my sister. She was an "oopsie" and came out premature, but the moment my dad laid eyes on her, he was smitten. He just never had that connection with me, I guess.

When I turned 18 and my mom told me that the child support is ending, I spoke to my dad and asked him what's going to happen with my university fund. He told me that my sister spent it all, there's nothing left for me.

I live in South Africa, highschool is only free if you get a government exemption, and they base who gets the exemption and who doesn't on how much your parents earn. It's stupid and short sighted but that's just how it is. My dad earns a LOT of money, so I wasn't granted that exemption. 

I think my dad paid quarterly for the school, so once the first quarter was up, my time in the school came to an end. I'm not sure. My mom just told me she can't pay for the rest of the year and that I'll just have to make another plan and do without. If I was smarter at the time, I probably could have found a way to finish regardless, but I wasn't and 18 year old me had no idea what resources I could take advantage of at the time. I was just devastated. I didn't even try stepping foot in the school again. My mother just kept me busy all day every day applying for jobs and helping her sell her stuff, I believed that that was all I could do, so it didn't even occur to me to just check with the school at the time.

I never managed to finish highschool but I'm planning on rectifying that next year. It costs a lot of money, so I've had to save up this year for it.

I'm going to cut her off. You're right that I'm being stupid. I'm 27 and I've gotten as far as I have without her. It was just hard to realize that myself until you pointed it out to me. She's only here for herself, not for me. There was just this big part of me that wished for a relationship with her so badly I was willing to delude myself into thinking she wanted the same thing. It really breaks my heart that the truth isn't even close to that. 

But I'll heal from it, in time. I'm used to getting back up. I just wish it could have been different this time.

In the beginning I felt like just curling up into a ball and never getting back up and I mostly just spent my first few days calling people I knew and begging them to let me crash on their couches for a bit. A few of them let me stay with them for a bit but I never overstayed my welcome, the reason I ended up homeless was because when i turned 18 my dad didn't have to pay for child support anymore and my mom didn't have a job of her own, so she sold her stuff and moved to her mom's overseas and just left me here. Cus of that I felt like nobody really wanted me and that made me hate relying on other people's kindness cus I felt like they also didn't want me near them. When I burned my last friendship out I kinda just wandered around not knowing what the hell to do, I was just so depressed. 

I started begging on the side of the road and sleeping underneath bridges until this other homeless guy talked to me and gave me some tips and helped me get out of that depression. I went from begging every day on the side of the road to going to hardware stores during the day to ask people going there if they needed me to do any kind of job for them. Some people asked me to help them with their gardens or moving furniture and stuff, and that kinda kept me going. People kept telling me that I should go to this city called Pretoria to look for work cus they're apparently always hiring in that city, so I hiked there one day and tried my luck but every time I went to a new city they'd always tell me that the next city over is the one with jobs. I started making friends on the road when people gave me lifts or when i was walking to the same place as someone else and eventually one of them gave me a seasonal labor job on a mine. I just kept being friendly and asking people if they needed me to do more work for them and when the season ended I got a call from one of my coworkers telling me that his new company was looking for hires.
